utterances.text: [In English] Thank you. [Interpretation] Is it correct that at the time, armed Muslims, rather than refer to them as members of the 28th Division of the BH Army, because that confuses you, wore the uniforms of the Ukraine battalion of UNPROFOR as well as civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They -- I saw a few of them wearing Ukraine uniforms, but they were not UNPROFOR Ukraine soldiers. So they had Ukraine uniforms, as I stated earlier in other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. I must have misunderstood it then.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Perhaps I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Sure.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I can emphasise that they were not wearing blue helmets or using white cars or any other UN symbols.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there were only camouflage uniforms that were the same as those worn by the Ukrainian battalion at Zepa; right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I asked them, one of them, "What kind of uniform are you wearing" and he said it was Ukraine. So I haven't seen a Ukraine uniform before and after, so I can only tell you what he told me. And I don't know whether he traded it in Zepa or how he really get it -- got it, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question in that respect. You said they were not wearing blue helmets, they were not wearing flak jackets, not using white cars. Were there any UN emblems on that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- uniform which was described to you as a Ukrainian uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: None at all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these same Muslims carried rocket launchers and a machine-gun at the time you saw them partly wearing Ukrainian uniforms and civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct. Say saw them carrying an RPG 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] They also had a machine-gun; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They also carried AKA 47 Kalashnikov rifles; right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that these armed Muslims opened fire from Kalashnikovs on you on that same occasion?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: On which -- are you still on the July 8th?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: On July 8th I only reported and remembered the grenade being thrown. So I don't know whether you -- you want another answer or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My mistake. Sorry. The next day. So it must be the 9th.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I was only -- when I left Bravo 1 to go to the marketplace to help the people who were there, the Bosnians who were on Bravo 1 thought that I was leaving them and they fired at our APC, and I think that's where you're referring to, and that happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think we've heard this firing at DutchBat leaving their positions several, several times. I -- is there any dispute about it? Mr. McCloskey says there's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was not clear whether this also happened on the 8th. Now it's clarified that it happened only on the 9th, so probably there is no dispute on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to focus on matters which are in dispute, but preferably do that after the break. Yes. We take another break of 20 minutes. Mr. Egbers, if you would follow the usher. We'll resume at 10 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I apologise about the confusion that I made concerning the 8th and 9th July 1995 and the events that happened on either of the dates. So now regardless of the dates, can you tell us if the members of the BH Army killed a member of the DutchBat on the day when you were fired at, or did it happen on some other day?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Do you want to know exactly when Raviv van Renssen was killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It must be in the files, because I don't know the exact date that he was killed, but he was killed by -- would you like me to confirm that he was killed by Bosnian Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I only want to establish whether, since we cannot establish it's 8th or 9th, is it the same day when it was shoot at you or some other day, if you can remember.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I'd have to look it up, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how you started your question, that -- I did not intervene there, but then the witness took you through some other matter which is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it correct and did you know that Captain Hageman's vehicle also came under fire from the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's discuss the 9th [Realtime transcript read in error "19th"] of July, 1995, now. In the Krstic case there is mention of Pusmulici close to Srebrenica. This was also mentioned today. Is it true that you did not have a view of this village, it wasn't within your view, and you were able to follow the clashes between the BH Army and the VRS by listening to the exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: We had a binocular that was able to give us a good view on the houses that were burned and people were going into the houses with dogs. I saw it and I described it, but we saw that because we had good vision at the village of Pusmulici in the south of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in order to avoid any confusion, we're talking about the 9th of July. The transcript says the 19th. That is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It is 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you able to see the fighting that went on in the village of Pusmulici between the Muslim and Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I haven't seen any fighting between the Muslim and Serb forces in that village. I only saw the people entering the houses and putting them on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in your testimony, Witness, that you also said something about taking goods from those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were other houses from Srebrenica, and I can't recall that in Pusmulici, because we saw, but I think you want to emphasise that there was fighting in this village, and I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I haven't seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Did you see that Muslim forces opened fire from the town of Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I remember that some Muslim fighters used the -- the gun on the APC of others. I've seen that. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Among other things. [Interpretation] On the 10th of July, 1991 [as interpreted], were you able to see that Muslim forces opened mortar fire while being among civilian population?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are transcribed as saying 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You meant 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are -- if you have to restart the question anyhow --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then I would like the witness to clarify what he means by the gun on the APC of others. Is that APCs not of Muslim fighters, of DutchBat? What are "others" in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an armed personnel carrier of the DutchBat that was in the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So are you referring to another -- something you have on paper where I -- where I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you if you saw the mortar opening fire from the centre of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I haven't seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I can ask Ms. Stewart to help us with one video that is evidence in this trial. It's V000-9265, and we need it from 5 minutes to 6 minutes, 36 seconds. Only minute and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, for what purpose, to establish that a mortar was fired? We have seen that video many times. What is the purpose of showing it now with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have a line of questions: If he knows, and how would he comment that the hole surrounding with civilians being around, whether that happened before or afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course you know that the Chamber is hesitant to hear the same evidence again and again and again. So if there's a good reason to elicit further evidence from this witness, of course you are -- please show it to him, and we'll find out at the end whether it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- served any purpose, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it will be -- that's why I cut it to only a minute and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we start, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before you put any questions, I put on the record that what was shown, V000-9265, is a part of P1147. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Colonel, did you know at that time, because you say you didn't see it, but did you receive a report that Muslim forces had opened mortar fire from the very centre of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you aware they opened fire on the 11th of July at the time when the column of civilians was moving from Srebrenica to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: The only thing I saw was that grenades were in the nearance of the refugees who were going from Srebrenica to Potocari. And when -- I was at the same spot at the day the refugees were there and I saw no mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time on the 11th, did you know where the bulk of the Muslim forces was?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: The only thing I knew at that time was that there were Muslim fighters going in the direction of Observation Post Alpha. So it's in the north-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time did you have information as to whether there was fighting around Srebrenica between Muslim and Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I have only seen Bosnian Serb tanks firing at the city. I have seen a few Muslim fighters trying to engage in the south of the enclave the Bosnian Serb Army, but I haven't seen man-to-man fights. I haven't seen a real defence of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During this shelling, as you say, next to the column, is it true that none of the civilians were wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I can't say that. I can only say that I saw the grenades fell in the left and the right of the column, and I haven't seen any killed people by that shelling. So I presumed it was there to keep them moving towards Potocari, but that was my assumption at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know today who opened that fire, Serb or Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was coming from the south, so it must be the BSA from the south of the -- of the town. And what I've learned today I can -- I can only tell you what I saw at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This mortar, was it in the southern or the northern part of the town, if you remember? And do you know in which direction it opened fire, or can you assess that from this video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What mortar? The mortar we saw on the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw the mortar standing near the gas station in the centre of Srebrenica, and as I -- I saw it firing at the south of the enclave. So I think at that time there were Bosnian Serb soldiers in the south of the enclave. But when I was there with my armed personnel carrier with all the refugees, I haven't seen any mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, is there any dispute about the position and the direction more or less of fire of that mortar?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of. I just -- it just appears to be what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then move on. We've seen it so many times, Mr. Lukic, and if something new comes up, if there's something this witness could tell us about -- well, first of all, he has not witnessed it, so the only thing he can do is tell us what he sees on the video, and we've heard that from other witnesses, and it's typically a matter which should be not subject of any dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I continue? I will change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, will you please keep this in the back of your mind if you continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it true, Colonel, that Muslims asked that you join them on their side with your APCs in their fight against the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Nobody asked me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the Muslims train the hand-held rocket launcher at your vehicle and demanded that your APC join the other four APCs that were in the southern part of the town?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I was ordered by my commander to leave Bravo 1 and join the other APCs at the marketplace. It was totally crowded that day. People with or without arms were outside not knowing what to do. And, yes, they aimed their gun at me. That's why I went out of the vehicle and tried to speak with them in -- in English. But I wasn't asked to join them. They pointed their RPG.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under that threat did you reposition your APC?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did. The next day I get the order to go back to Bravo 1 again, and my commander told me that I had to prepare for an air-strike, as he called it, and that's what I told the Muslim fighters who were at the marketplace at the time, that I had to go back to Bravo 1 for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you knew there would be an attack against Serb positions by the NATO Air Force, and for that reason you had to return to your previous position from the Bravo observation post?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's true. And I had a forward air controller who was in contact with -- with the -- with the pilots.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the task of that DutchBat member, this forward air controller?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: He could point out the targets that were shooting at us. So he tried to point out the tanks, T-54, T-55 that were shooting at UN positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did these forward air controllers establish communication with the pilot?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, but only with the close-air support fighters that came on very late that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that two Dutch F16 aircraft on that occasion made two Serb tanks unusable, unserviceable?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether they -- the two tanks were unusable, but I know that they didn't fire at us any more so I could go back to Srebrenica town. So, yes, they dropped bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned in your previous testimony members of the SAS. You called them Jim and Dave; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know how they came to Srebrenica, who sent them? They were not members of the DutchBat, were they?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: No, but they were special forces, and they joined our special forces, and they were in the enclave for months. I don't know whether they were there when we arrived in January 1995. Could be. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they have any role in guiding NATO aeroplanes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Not from my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did other members of the SAS in May, June, July come to Srebrenica with the role of guiding NATO aeroplanes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I only saw these two, and they were with our battalion for a long period of time, and we brought our own forward air controllers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you a few questions to clarify. You were asked whether the SAS members had any role in guiding NATO aeroplanes. You said, "Not from my position," which leaves open that you do not know about other positions or that you know that it was not from your position but they did from other positions. Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- I know that special forces, Dutch special forces, with radio contact with the fighters went in other positions. So I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there for a second because I think we were talking about SAS persons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't seen the SAS, and I don't know whether they had any contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever their role was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever their role was, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's the first question. We needed some clarification. Then you were asked about other members of the SAS, whether they came with the role of guiding NATO aeroplanes. You said, "I only saw these two, and they were with our battalion for a long period of time and we brought our own forward air controllers," which is still not an answer to the question. The question was whether the SAS people had come with the role of guiding NATO aeroplanes. If you know, please tell us. If you don't know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We shall move to the 11th of July. Just let us finish first something concerning the 10th regarding this video. After that, I'll ask you something else. Would you agree that opening mortar fire from this environment with many civilians in immediate vicinity was mainly geared at provoking Serb fire for the purpose of causing civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I would not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you as a soldier allow your troops to open fire at enemy positions while being surrounded by civilians?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you again. You earlier said you did not agree with what Mr. Lukic put to you, that the opening mortar fire was mainly geared at provoking Serb fire for the purpose of causing civilian casualties. Now, you did not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: However, would you agree if Mr. Lukic would have asked you that it created considerable risks by doing that for the civilian population surrounding you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That, of course, is true, but I don't think that they fired the mortar in order to provoke the Bosnian Serb Army to shell them back. I think they wanted to use the weapon in stopping the troops to enter the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With a considerable risk that nevertheless return fire would be opened and would hit at, if aimed at the source of fire, then that there was a considerable risk that the civilian population would severely suffer from that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's certainly true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, I took it that that is the issue you wanted to explore.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I want to thank you for posing additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, members of the Dutch Battalion moved civilians from Srebrenica to Potocari; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Most of the people walked from Srebrenica to Potocari when they saw it was safe to go there, but we didn't move them with buses or other vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you personally get orders to join the action of moving the civilians?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I get the orders to go back to Potocari to see if it was safe, so we were on the front of all the people who followed us carrying all the wounded from the hospital in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among the Dutch soldiers, you were at the tail end of the column; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: No. I was more in the front of the column. I wasn't on the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Because the Dutch report, although it was not under oath, says that you testified you were at the tail end of the column. But in any case, you did not see any Muslim civilian killed while this was happening?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Upon arriving at Potocari, you slept the following 12 hours because you were exhausted. You hadn't slept for days before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes. We transported all the sick and wounded from the hospital to our hospital, and then I had a short rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you a few things about the 12th of July, 1995. That day you received orders to go to the convoy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: At that day, I escorted the first convoy to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the front of the column there was Major Boering and one captain; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You controlled the tail end of the column, and you had a good field of vision. You could see the entire convoy; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You described seeing in Bratunac - I believe it's Bratunac. You'll correct me if I'm wrong - seeing people shouting and throwing things at the convoy; that is to say, Serbs standing outside the trucks and the buses throwing objects at your convoy.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you saw people around the convoy throwing things at buses and trucks? Did you see the hostile sentiment around the convoy?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was a hostile sentiment, but they're all -- there was also a party going on. Everybody was celebrating. So it was a very confusing situation, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At any rate, you passed through safely, and together with all the other members of the convoy you arrived safely at Kladanj; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Well, I described that one of the buses broke down, that I was there with the buses -- with a single bus, and the other buses went to Kladanj, and then we -- we went to a point where people get out of the bus as described in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, you described it.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: So what is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the safe passage of the convoy -- or, rather, you informed the Papa Observation Post of the safe arrival of the convoy at Kladanj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's right. But I had no -- I can't guarantee the safety of all the buses where I wasn't driving along with these buses. I was there with one of the buses who broke down. So when I went to the point where all the people had to get out in Kladanj, they had to walk, and I counted the buses, but I don't know what happened on the way, if somebody stopped a bus or did something with the people inside the bus. I don't know. Perhaps you know. Things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you did have a radio set with you in the vehicle, seeing that you were able to inform the Papa OP about it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now it was the OP Alpha that you informed of the arrival of a different convoy, the one that you escorted on the following day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: OP Alpha was in the west of the -- of the enclave, so I think it's -- I'm sure that I'm in contact with one of the two observation posts, and could be Alpha as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I again remind you that over the last couple of minutes about this first escort and the safe arrival, your questions do not add anything at all to what is already in the testimony given before which is now in evidence. I mean, if evidence is presented in the way it was done by the Prosecution, where there's no hint even at not arriving safely at Kladanj, then there's no need to further -- further explore that. I mean -- because the Chamber, reading that evidence, will read nothing of the safety being jeopardised at any point in time there. And if I read it in the way you sought the witness to repeat it. Yes. We come now to the next day. Perhaps you have something new about the radio equipment. We knew already as well, because the witness said we used that later when the car was taken so that they had radio equipment with them is clear from the evidence also. So let's now move on to the next day, and let's try to get something what adds for the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to ask you about the availability of water for the people in Potocari. Can we now call up 1D35 in e-court. Before the document comes up, let me tell you that it's a telegram sent by Mr. Akashi to Mr. Kofi Annan relating to Srebrenica. Did Mr. Akashi receive information through UNPROFOR channels from the DutchBat in Srebrenica? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise. There is no document 1D35 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see 65 ter number 15738.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you will see, it's a telegram sent to Mr. Annan by Mr. Akashi from the UNPROFOR HQ in Zagreb. It was on the 12th July 1995. We'll need the next page. Item number 4, the first paragraph on the page. The last portion of it, four lines from the bottom it reads: [In English] "The drinking-water source for Potocari has not been cut off by the Serbs, and thus water is available for the people. However, the overcrowded conditions combined with the lack of shelter facilities are quickly creating sanitation problems which will result in public health problems." [Interpretation] Would you accept this report by Mr. Akashi that the Serbs had not cut off any water supplies and that the Muslims in Potocari had water available to them?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt this, but I haven't -- I haven't heard about any water supplies cutting off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You discussed the problem and you said that you provided civilians with water, we do accept that, but we'd like to ask you if you knew that there was another water source which the civilians in Potocari were able to use at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I didn't provide anyone with water. It wasn't in my previous testimonies. So I gave -- we -- we had -- so were you referring to -- because I didn't do anything with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we then -- because there are two elements apparently in this report. First that it was not -- the water source was not cut by the Serbs. You said, well, I have no reason to have any doubt. You have no knowledge that it would have been.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the second part of this sentence is: "And thus water is available to the people." Were you aware of any shortage of water at that moment in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that we gave all the water we had for drinking water to the people, but -- and I think -- I mean, one day we ran out of water that is usable for drinking immediately. So that's what I recall at that time. So I don't know whether those people couldn't go to the river to drink. We had some toilets on the compound of Potocari, but people didn't dare to use it. They wanted their own shelter. So I don't know if it is clear, but it was it was 35 degrees Celsius at that day, and people had to drink a lot of water, of course. So I wasn't there giving water to the people, others did that, and I -- I see that there is a source of water but I don't know whether we could use them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you don't know about that source.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you know whether the source was such that it would be able to sufficiently supply the water needed at that moment? Did you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about the white house, as you called it, in relation to 12 and 13 July, 1995. Would you agree that you saw people on the white house on the 13th of July, 1995, that's to say on the second day of evacuation, and that you didn't see anyone in the white house on the 12th of July, 1995, that's to say on the first day of evacuation?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I have been there only at the second day of the evacuation, and then I visited the white house in the morning, early in the morning, and then I saw all these people going into convoy 3. And the first date of the evacuation when I was in the first convoy, I haven't seen anything at the white house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I again seek clarification. If you say, "I haven't seen anything at the white house," that is -- there is some ambiguity there. It could mean I haven't been in the white house and therefore I don't see anything in the white house. The other thing is that I've been in the white house but I didn't see anything. Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the first one because I was with the first convoy to leave Potocari, so I -- all those people were there, and there came 14, 15 buses inside the enclave and Bosnian Serbs put all the people -- put the first buses, they filled them with people, so we had to go after the last bus of the first convoy. On the second day, the Bosnian Serbs were using the house to -- to gather all the men and boys that were trying to leave with the buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the first day you just haven't been there and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- cannot tell us anything about what may have been seen by those who were there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Upon your insistence you were able to enter the white house. Is it correct that you saw quite a few knives outside the house that had been taken from the people who were inside the house?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but they were knives where you can cut an apple with. I think everybody has one. So there were no big knives, but I saw them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you be transporting people in possession of such knives? Had you been the warring part against the Muslim side, or would you, too, have taken these knives from them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hypothetical question, Mr. Lukic. If the witness wants to answer that's fine, but what he would have done under similar circumstances. Of course, a question is would you consider this to be a risk. That is a question which asks for the knowledge of the witness and it's not hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It is a very small risk. The people I saw there were very ill, elderly people, 60 -- 50, 60 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Is it a rule -- or, rather, do the rules of the Dutch army dictate that men of the opposing warring party be searched and frisked before they are transported anywhere and that the process any type of weapon has to be seized?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Well, the men that were inside the house didn't belong to an opposing warring party, as you referred. They were just refugees in Srebrenica, Potocari, wanted to leave the enclave with their families in buses. So it's not -- you try to make an image that there are Muslim fighters among the people in the white house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Egbers, you are more or less entering in a debatement with Mr. Lukic on his questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not what you're supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're challenging the picture he wishes to create. We leave that to Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is whether there were any rules of the Dutch army dictating the search of persons, may I say so, you want to transport. We leave alone whether they're members of the -- well, let's say if they were of the warring party. I would say the question if they were, there's no need to dispute that. That's what Mr. Lukic put in this question, whether there are such rules do exist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The rules we exist are the Geneva Conventions, of course, and when you are a part of an armed force that you get treated well, but you get searched, sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there was general mobilisation in force at the time in Srebrenica which applied to all men aged between 16 and 60?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness about the white house again. In one of your answers, I'm not sure if the transcript gives the right answer, on page 66, line 19 I read: "It is a very small risk. The people I saw there were very ill, elderly people, 60 -- 50, 60 years old."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Old people, I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Not ill.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not ill people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is what I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- thought that I would have elicited. Another question in that respect: Can you describe the situation in the white house as you saw it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my intention was there because there were families screaming because their men were taken from them and transported to the white house, so I came there and I asked the Bosnian Serbs and my own soldiers who were there, I said, "What's indeed the house?" And then they said, "Well, we don't know because we can't enter." And so then I tried being a first lieutenant to enter the house, and I pointed at my rank and I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What did you see in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went into the house, I saw men sitting in several chambers waiting, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Waiting in chairs, on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How many people did you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time it wasn't very crowded. It was early in the morning. But when I was there around 11.00 when all the buses were filled with the men from the white house, there were three buses full of men. So there were, let's say, 150, perhaps even more men. But at the time I visited the house, it wasn't crowded at all and they were -- everybody was alive at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did the house have a balcony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't really recall that right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did the people in the white house have their personal belongings with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I saw a lot of personal belongings in the garden of the -- in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did any of the soldiers of the Bosnian Serb army tell you what the purpose of detaining the people in this house was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They told me that they wanted to search them, and they pointed at the knives they found, and they wanted to interrogate them, try to get them to Kladanj as well to exchange them for Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What was the purpose of interrogating them, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know at that time, but they -- they considered them as opposing forces, and I considered them as all the men who wanted to leave the enclave with their family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you see anybody preparing lists of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you see any IDs of these people somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't seen them, but my colleague, he saw them in the same garden where I saw all the gear they took with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think it's time for a break. We'll take a break of 20 minutes. You may follow the usher, and we'll continue at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, two hours you asked for to give an answer to my question whether there's still a need to cross-examine Kathryn Barr, where you do not oppose the admission of the report. You said give me two hours. I gave you two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was hoping you forgot it. I was just informed by my colleague who was more familiar with Ms. Barr's report, since he had it in another trial, and we don't ask for cross-examination of Ms. Barr.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the report can be admitted and without cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can it be 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. You're right, Mr. Lukic, it's for us to discuss under what Rule exactly we will admit or -- the report, because there's no objection against admission, and no cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, can you tell us what role members of the DutchBat had in registering the people at Potocari, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I only know that Major Franken, who was a deputy battalion commander at that time, made a list of I think 275 men who were on the compound under his -- or he registered them. Is that the list you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I know that it was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know the age of the people who were registered by Major Franken?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of role the DutchBat members had, if any, in putting people up in the white house?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I don't know whether we had any role at all. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in agreement with the Geneva Conventions, civilians should be separated from soldiers.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We discussed the white house, and I'd like to go back to an issue. You were answering to questions by His Honour Judge Fluegge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we change subject, you asked whether the witness agrees that in agreement with the Geneva Conventions civilians should be separated from soldiers. This is a rather vague question. Do you mean in a combat situation, or do you mean when combatants are taken prisoner they should not be mixed up with civilians, or -- the context, it came immediately after the white house. It's totally unclear to me, but perhaps you can ask the witness how he understood the question, what you were referring to. Perhaps you could first ask the witness how he understood the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understood the question as a general question, whether the civilian people needed extra protection, and that is what is in the Geneva Conventions. So when you are part of a force and you're recognisable as a force, then you should be treated different than the -- the refugees and the normal population. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's now -- it's still not entirely clear to me. I mean, in a combat situation --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you may have to evacuate civilians perhaps under the convention -- conventions in order to avoid that they become affected by the combat operations, whereas if we're talking about treated differently from refugees and the normal position, that sounds more like in a position where the combatants have laid down their weapons or aren't perhaps hors de combat. So it's still rather unclear to me, but I leave it if that's -- if you feel your question is answered by that, Mr. Lukic, then I will invite you to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will then return a bit to that question, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, is it correct that there were very few uniformed and armed individuals in the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 9th, 10th, and 11th of July in Srebrenica, were you able to see armed individuals in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There were no men armed with firearms in Potocari; right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: You refer at the families who gathered around the compound?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I haven't seen any armed men with the families gathering in the neighbourhood of the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you therefore agree with me that the membership of the Muslim armed forces could not be established by the fact that somebody was armed or wore a uniform or was in civilian clothes? There was no way for someone to see with the naked eye without additional checks whether somebody was a member of the Muslim armed forces or not?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen any brigade, Muslim armed brigade, in Potocari or Srebrenica. I have seen refugees, I have seen the original population over there, and I have seen some men carrying arms, but they were communicating with small notes. But I didn't have any idea that there was an armed force trying to reject the Bosnian Serb Army. I haven't -- I know what you are referring to, but I haven't seen any army of the -- of the Muslims inside the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Would you be surprised to see that there are documents on the Muslim side which stated that there were between 4- and 6.000 armed men in Srebrenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I would be very surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll show you one such document in a minute or so. I'd like to go back to the white house again. You said that you didn't see anyone getting killed in it. Would you agree with me that you didn't see anyone being beaten up either?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I haven't any recollection of any beaten-up person inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that the convoy set off from the white house consisting of three buses. You did tell us who escorted the convoy, but I can't remember at this time. Was it your colleague Versteeg?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That is what -- that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you or did you learn some other way about who it was who stopped the convoy and changed its direction, and do you know anything about the initial course that the convoy took?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I only know that he was stopped, there was a gun pointed at his head, and he had to turn around. That was all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to the 13th of July, 1995. You said that you escorted the convoy on that day as well, evacuating people from Potocari. On the 13th of July, 1995, you saw men boarding buses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I haven't seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What day was it then that this convoy set off that your colleague Versteeg escorted?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was on the first day, but I don't really understand the question, because we had two days of evacuation, more days of evacuation. The first day I was on the first convoy. The second day I was on convoy number four, went to Kladanj, and stopped at Nova Kasaba. So I wasn't with the men. I was with the women and children in convoy 4. So I haven't seen any men coming into the buses. I wasn't with -- with the three buses of men that went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I apologise then.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will skip these questions then. I'd like to discuss the 13th and the 14th of July, 1995, at Nova Kasaba. One part of the day of the 13th of July you spent at Nova Kasaba; right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: In the afternoon, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to call up in e-court 1D1042. What we have before us is a form. Let me first ask you this: This form, which is in English, does it contain your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is something that was unclear to me about your stay there and Major Malinic. Do you recall filling out this form?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Not by date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you do remember answering these questions and filling it out?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Well, I don't have this chart, but it's a form handed over to me in Zagreb. It could be we went to Zagreb and had to fill out this form there right -- right after we arrived. Could be. I don't know. Is it -- do you know whether it's dated?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I don't have date with me. But if you can see -- maybe it's on the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. So I think it was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: What is the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you were not taken prisoner on that occasion by the Serb forces? You were free to leave, but the Army of Republika Srpska could not guarantee safety to you. That was question number 3 on this form, and you can refresh your memory as to what your answer was at the time.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes. We were stopped with our cars near the school, guns were pointed at us. We had to step out of the vehicles, and then we had to stay there because nobody could guarantee our safety. So we were able to sleep in the building, to walk around the school, but of course we were not in a position to go back to the enclave if we wanted. That's what we tried to do, but the -- the Mercedes that we used for that -- and we drove a few hundred metres, and then they were stopped by people who pointed their guns at our colleagues and took their cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that, you go back to the school again where Major Malinic was present; right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this form, you describe having been his guest -- guests. Would you agree with that description?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes. He tried to make it as comfortable for me as he could. He even played chess with me. He wanted to play chess, and he invited me. So it's a very strange situation in a wartime where you're held at a school and this major wants to play chess and wants to have dinner and wants to speak with me about -- about the situation in his country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where can we find a reference to a Major Malinic and the treatment as a guest, the treatment of the witness as a guest?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since there is no numbers, I counted answers, and it should be answer number 4. The first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- is number 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What page, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's English page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And B/C/S page 2 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we should move to that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first one is question number 3 where it says: "We were not captured. We were free to go." And the latest one is the next one: "We were guests of the BSA, CO Major Malinic, Zoran." And then there is the last paragraph on this page if you can see it. Yes. The whole paragraph. It says: "All the BSA personnel tried to guarantee our safety. Driving a white car wasn't safe. B and H and BSA could fire."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And we also can see more at the top of the page like you referred to the sentence "We were not captured." At the end of that answer or the entry, there is the sentence: "We tried to drive back with three UN Mercedes. After 500 metres, two of them were stolen."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the witness just confirmed it for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And therefore, I've read it into the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then on page 3, fourth question as I counted it, there is only one "No," and the question was: "Were you physically attacked or maltreated by your captors at that time?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it correct that at that time while you were at the headquarters of Major Malinic nobody mistreated you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just offer this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1042 receives number D307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will now move to a different topic. In your evidence, you describe the shooting by Serbian forces at the forest, and you said there was no gunfire coming from the forest, and you spoke about that on page 2236 in your testimony of 5th April 2000 in the Krstic case. You said you hadn't heard any gunfire coming from the woods at Serb positions. However, at that time, did you know at all whether there were any Muslims in the place at which the Serb forces were shooting? Were you able to know whether they were shooting at the forest, at an empty space, or enemy soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I have only heard a gun -- a machine-gun firing in the woods. I didn't hear a fire-fight, a fight between two people. So one is shooting and the other one is reacting. It was just single shooting in the forest. So it was by machine-guns. Normally when you have a fight you can hear one or two shots and then a reaction of the other side. So that's what I asked this Major Malinic the next morning, about the shooting, and he said, "Well, I have very young soldiers, and when they hear something, they'll start shooting at anything they hear."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My colleague, my learned friend is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. The section that was referred to from the Krstic testimony was about firing into the woods between Sandici and Nova Kasaba, when he was on the road, where he saw soldiers deployed along that road, and I think the witness is speaking about an entirely different set of firing that he heard when he was at the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least you invite Mr. Lukic to clarify whether it is a different thing or whether it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was asking about Sandici and Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But can you check the reference again? I don't find the portion on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 2236. No, I don't find it there. Not exactly what you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's line 15, 16, and 17, maybe, if I'm not mistaken. But we can have 1D1040 in the e-court if you want to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was a question at these lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I have the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No. The question was put to the witness: "Now, at least on this part of the journey did you hear any firing coming out of the woods in the direction of those soldiers? "A. No, sir, I did not."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I was -- yes, that's the portion. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but it's not clear to me whether the witness was in fact providing an answer to that question in relation to Sandici, to Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you mean now or then?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, not then in Krstic. Today, just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just now. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Should I answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. So I thought that -- that -- that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. So I thought that Mr. Lukic was referring to shooting during the night when I was at Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And whereas the portion read to you was on your trip --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- where you said: "I saw from Sandici until Nova Kasaba every 3 metres a few soldiers," and then you said something about shooting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was totally different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's totally different from how you understand --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How you understood the question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you answered. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you to my learned friend, and can we now clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Colonel, please, can you answer this question, whether -- have you ever seen Serbian soldiers shooting in the direction of -- on that trip into the -- the opposite side --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I have seen them shooting at the forest at the direction of the enclave when I drove by over the same road that the soldiers were standing. I couldn't see them shooting people. Is that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In fact, I have just one more question for you regarding the 14th of July, 1995, and I will finish earlier than I had planned. You saw the Muslim forces open fire at Serb positions on the 14th of July, 1995, at Nova Kasaba; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I only heard two shots at the school. I haven't seen anybody firing them, but this Major Malinic told me that they were shooting at the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did any action ensue? Did they try to pursue the assailants? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes. They pointed the anti-aircraft gun at the position, then they had 20 or 25 men gathered, and they took two boys out of the house, two Muslim boys, which they used as a human shield, and they drove them in front of them trying to catch the forces or the -- or the people that shot the two rounds at the school. And after a time they came back, they had no success, and the two boys were still alive and they were put back in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, thank you for answering my questions. That was all I had for you today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the last question was again both question and answer completely repetitious from the testimony, but, Mr. Lukic -- Ms. Hasan, do you have any questions or re-examination for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Very briefly one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Simply a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: At today's transcript at the end of transcript page 74, beginning of transcript page 75, there was a question about on the 13th of July did you see men boarding buses, and you answered: "I haven't seen that." And I think the lead-up to that might have been a bit confusing given your previous testimony today and in Krstic. So when you left on convoy 4 on the 13th of July, was that the same day that convoy 3 left which carried the men who were on the three buses that you saw come out of the white house onto the buses and leave to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Egbers, this then concludes your testimony in this court. We were informed that you were postponed a couple of times. We're nevertheless happy that you came today and that we were able to conclude -- complete your testimony today. Thank you for coming. Thank you for having answered all the questions that you were put to you by the parties and the Bench. You're excused, and you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's not sufficient time to continue with the previous witness. I would say, if I may have been a bit grumpy now and then on repetitious questions, then I think it's only fair that I also put on the record that it's appreciated that the parties did their utmost best and finished the completed testimony of this witness today. I think in all fairness that should be said as well. We -- six minutes before the usual time we adjourn, and we adjourn and will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 27th of June, in this same Courtroom I at 9.30 in the morning.
